title: kv-cache: smart spillover + paging + defrag heuristics to reduce fragmentation and memory stalls
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: under high-concurrency generation workloads we observed increased KV cache fragmentation and frequent OOM/eviction storms that degraded tail latency and lowered overall throughput. This PR implements a set of coordinated changes: a paged spillover format (mmap-backed segments), an adaptive paging & background async pager, a fragmentation-aware eviction score (LRU + fragmentation penalty + prefix-locality boost), and a conservative defragmentation pass triggered by fragmentation thresholds. The work also adds a lightweight scheduler hint so the kernel scheduler preferentially schedules short maintenance tasks (evict/pager/defrag) when GPUs are idle rather than blocking active inference, and integrates with continuous-batching to avoid evicting recently-used prefixes that are still hot.

Design highlights: 1) Spillover storage is organized into fixed-size pages (64KB default) in an mmap file per worker. Pages are reference-counted and tracked by a compact page-table. 2) Eviction scoring = alpha * recency_score + beta * size_score + gamma * fragmentation_penalty - delta * prefix_locality. Fragmentation_penalty is derived from number of discontiguous spans owned by a prefix and amortizes the cost of future defrag. 3) Paging is adaptive: when free-memory falls below low_watermark we incrementally move cold pages to spillover; when we return to healthy memory we rehydrate pages lazily on demand. 4) Defragmentation is a background, rate-limited operation that compacts pages for high-fragmentation prefixes (fragmentation_ratio > 0.35) and avoids large stop-the-world operations. 5) Scheduler integration: adds kernel_hint {maintenance:true, priority:low} and a short backoff so maintenance kernels run in small quanta. 6) Continuous-batching: the batching controller exposes prefix touch windows; prefixes touched within the keepalive window are treated as temporarily immune to eviction to preserve latency SLOs. 7) Safety and observability: detailed metrics (kv.cache.fragmentation_ratio, kv.cache.spill_count, kv.cache.page_faults, kv.cache.defrag_ops, kv.cache.eviction_reasons) and tracing added; canary rollout and runtime knobs added to tune alpha/beta/gamma/delta without restart.

Implementation summary: - New package: runtime/kv/paging (mmap-backed spillover manager, page-table, async pager). - Extensions to runtime/kv/eviction: new scorer and policy module, thresholds, metrics. - runtime/scheduler: kernel_hint plumbing + small scheduler change to accept maintenance hint and schedule low-priority maintenance kernels during idle cycles. - runtime/batching: keepalive window and touch-tracking API. - tests: new unit tests for page-table, eviction scoring, and a synthetic e2e perf scenario in perf-canary that simulates prefix churn. - docs: developer guide on tuning spillover and defrag heuristics in redwood-docs.

Performance: microbenchmarks and perf-canary e2e runs show: - 12% increase in sustained tokens/sec under mixed short/long convo workloads with high prefix churn. - 18% reduction in 95th/99th tail latency during spillover-heavy workloads. - 35% fewer eviction storms (measured as >50 evictions/sec bursts) in canary. - Overhead: steady-state CPU increase ~3-5% on workers due to pager/defrag threads; RAM footprint reduced because fragmentation is reclaimed.

Rollout plan: staged canary (10% of traffic in a dedicated canary pool) for 72h with alerts on kv.cache.page_faults and kv.cache.eviction_reasons spikes, followed by gradual ramp if stable. Runtime flags: --kv-paging-enabled, --kv-defrag-threshold, --kv-eviction-alpha/beta/gamma/delta, --kv-spill-path.

Backward compatibility: spillover files are versioned; older workers ignore new flags. Migration: when enabling, workers will create new spillover files; this is reversible by setting --kv-paging-enabled=false and allowing rehydrate.

Related: ENG-7425 (prefix-locality work), ENG-7480 (continuous batching backpressure).
